Rhagaea raises the late emperor's bloodstained mantle once more, accusing the northern Senate of complicity in his death. Lucon denies the charge, claiming the south is exploiting an old crime to seize the throne.
Now the southern eagle standards advance north. The truth remains uncertain, but an old grievance has become a new war.

After a long campaign, neither side has secured a decisive advantage. Exhausted armies return to their camps as envoys agree to suspend the fighting.
The accusations surrounding the emperor's death remain unresolved. The treaty quiets the border, but does not settle the grievance.
